title: robustness-shear-test-catalog-and-onboarding-checklist-2026
author: Maya Rao
summary: A concise catalog of targeted "shear" tests designed to surface brittle failure modes during model onboarding. Includes a prescriptive onboarding checklist, sample test configs, acceptance thresholds, and a lightweight triage runbook for failed checks.
body:
Overview:
This document defines a catalog of robustness "shear" tests (targeted perturbation experiments) and an associated onboarding checklist for promoting models into Redwood's serving fleets. The objective is to detect brittle or non-linear failure modes that standard holistic evaluations miss (e.g., sudden output degradation under minor tokenization changes, KV-cache boundary conditions, quantization-sensitive artifacts, or throughput-induced truncation).

Motivation:
- Standard metrics (perplexity, static accuracy) can hide regime-specific failures.
- Production traffic has micro-patterns (short bursts, long context prefixes, partial cache hits) that interact with optimization paths (KV cache reuse, kernel selection, quantized activation ranges).
- Early detection reduces rollback risk and costly customer incidents.

Scope and audience:
- Intended consumers: Model owners, inference engineers, applied ML evaluators, and SREs responsible for onboarding models to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private channels.
- Not in scope: annotation tooling, full audit logs for compliance artifacts (see model-promotion docs for that flow).

Shear Test Catalog (categories and canonical examples):
1) Tokenization Shear
   Purpose: Detect brittle behavior caused by small tokenization shifts (whitespace, hyphenation, unusual punctuation).
   Inputs: 2k canonical prompts + deterministic perturbation functions (insert/remove spaces, zero-width chars, alternate quotes).
   Primary metrics: Top-1 label change rate, semantic similarity (BERTScore), and length ratio of outputs.
   Failure threshold: >6% semantic change rate or average similarity drop >0.07 vs baseline.

2) Context-Shear (prefix and suffix boundary conditions)
   Purpose: Surface failures when useful context is truncated, repeated, or includes repeated delimiters that affect KV cache and attention masks.
   Inputs: variable-length prefixes (0, 128, 512, 2048 tokens), repeated-system-message sequences, long trailing whitespace.
   Metrics: Stability index (fraction of identical answer intents), token-budget latency multiplier, correctness for deterministic prompts.
   Failure threshold: stability index < 0.92 for deterministic intent prompts; >1.4x median token latency multiplier at long prefix length.

3) KV-Cache Shear
   Purpose: Evaluate correctness and performance when requests reuse partial KV cache entries or when cache keys are evicted between related requests.
   Inputs: grouped conversational sequences with planned cache evictions and partial history truncation.
   Metrics: Response divergence after cache eviction, error-rate in incremental continuation.
   Failure threshold: >3% divergence in final answer surface area after eviction for stateful workloads.

4) Quant-Shear
   Purpose: Expose error modes introduced by quantized kernels and dequantization rounding (especially for edge-case activation distributions).
   Inputs: representative workloads instrumented for activation distribution sampling and worst-case prompt generators (low-entropy vs high-entropy).
   Metrics: Delta in task accuracy/F1, hallucination rate, distributional shift in logits per-layer.
   Failure threshold: task metric drop >2% absolute OR consistent hallucination increase (relative +25%).

5) Throughput & Burst Shear
   Purpose: Confirm model quality and latencies under bursty traffic and mixed-size batching.
   Inputs: synthetic burst schedule (Poisson + heavy-tail spikes), mixed sequence-length mix.
   Metrics: 95/99 latency percentiles, tail error rates, model selection fallback incidence.
   Failure threshold: p99 latency exceeds SLO by >20% OR error rate rises above error-budget allowance for the test window.

6) Linguistic Adversarial Shear
   Purpose: Discover subtle prompt-engineering corner cases (code-mixed inputs, heavy token overlap with stop sequences, counterfactual reasoning tricks).
   Inputs: curated adversarial prompt bank (50k seeds) with transformations (negation flips, role-play inversion).
   Metrics: Semantic flip rate, toxic/harmful output signal increase.
   Failure threshold: semantic flip >5% on high-confidence prompts OR increase in policy-alerting signals beyond baseline.

Canonical test config schema (human-readable example):
- test_name: tokenization-shear-basic
- workload: completion_deterministic_v1
- samples: 2000
- perturbations: ["insert_zero_width_space", "replace_smart_quotes", "collapse_double_space"]
- metrics: ["semantic_similarity", "top1_label_change"]
- run_profile: {parallelism: 50, tokens_limit: 1024, repeat_seed: 42}

(Example JSON snippet for CI integration)
```
{
  "test_name": "tokenization-shear-basic",
  "workload": "completion_deterministic_v1",
  "samples": 2000,
  "perturbations": ["insert_zero_width_space","replace_smart_quotes","collapse_double_space"],
  "metrics": ["semantic_similarity","top1_label_change"],
  "run_profile": "parallelism:50;tokens_limit:1024;seed:42"
}
```

Onboarding Checklist (step-by-step):
1) Preflight (owner)
   - Register model metadata in model-catalog (name, architecture, quant profile candidates, expected max_context).
   - Attach representative small-batch sample of customer traffic (or synthetic proxy) and tokenization baseline.

2) Baseline Evals (evaluator)
   - Run standard eval battery (accuracy suites, prompt-coverage matrix).
   - Record baseline metrics and embeddings for semantic-stability comparisons.

3) Shear Test Runs (evaluator + infra)
   - Execute full Shear Test Catalog (Tokenization, Context, KV-Cache, Quant, Throughput, Linguistic Adversarial).
   - Save raw traces: logits-per-layer (sampled), latency histograms, kernel selection logs, quant dequant counters.

4) Analyze & Triangulate (owner + SRE)
   - Compare to baseline; generate a per-test report with delta metrics and a short explanation of potential root causes (e.g., tokenization mapping mismatch, quant overflow in layer 7).
   - For any failing test, classify severity (A=blocking, B=investigate before canary, C=monitor in canary).

5) Mitigation & Re-run (engineering)
   - Apply mitigations: swap quant profile, pin tokenizer normalization, reduce sequence packing, or increase KV-cache sensitivity window.
   - Re-run failing tests to verify improvement.

6) Promotion Gate (product + infra)
   - Only models with zero A-severity failures AND no more than one B-severity (with documented mitigation and rollback plan) proceed to canary.

Acceptance criteria (numerical):
- Tokenization Shear: semantic similarity drop <= 0.07; top-1 label flip rate <= 6%.
- Context Shear: intent-stability >= 0.92 for deterministic prompts; latency multiplier <= 1.4 at max_context.
- Quant Shear: task metric drop <= 2% absolute; hallucination rate relative increase <= 25%.
- Throughput Shear: p99 latency <= SLO * 1.2; error-rate rise <= 0.5% absolute.

Lightweight Triage Runbook (when a test fails):
1) Reproduce locally with the failing sample and the same random seed.
2) Inspect kernel selection and quant profile logs for the failing request. Look for non-deterministic kernel swaps or saturating activations.
3) Run per-layer activation histogram on the failing input and compare with baseline histograms.
4) If quant-related: try next-safe quant profile (e.g., from int8-optim to int8-stable) or float16 fallback and re-evaluate failing cases.
5) If cache-related: re-run with full-history and with history-stripped variations to confirm the cache delta.
6) Document the root cause hypothesis and mitigation plan in the model-catalog entry; escalate to runtime-kernel if low-level bug suspected.

Operationalizing in CI and Canary:
- CI: Integrate each shear test as a stage in model PR validation. Tokenization and linguistic adversarial tests are fast-path (run on every PR). Heavy-throughput and KV-cache tests run nightly or per-release.
- Canary: For models passing acceptance criteria, execute a reduced shear subset (representative tokenization and quant checks) during canary with real traffic sampling. Monitor 'Shear Regression' dashboard for sudden drift.

Dashboard and Alerts (suggested):
- Shear Regression dashboard: per-test delta sparklines, failing-test list, p99 latency split by prefix length.
- Alerts: open ticket if any A-severity failure appears in CI or if canary shows >2% regression on acceptance metrics within 24h.

Owners and contacts:
- Default owner: Model Onboarding Team (model-onboarding@redwood.ai)
- Primary contact for quantization triage: Ethan Park (eng-serving-runtime)
- Runtime kernel escalation: Kernel Team Pager duty (see eng-serving-runtime/team-wiki)

Appendix: Quick CLI examples
- Run a single shear test locally (example):
  cli run-shear --test tokenization-shear-basic --model-path gs://models/my-model/v1 --out results/token-shear-v1.json --seed 42

- Minimal retrace command to collect activation histograms for a failing example:
  cli collect-activation --model gs://models/my-model/v1 --example-id 1234 --layers 0-11 --out /tmp/act-1234.json
